overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving insufficiently detailed May 8, 2023 minutes that omitted the complainant's statement and two unsummarized discussions; it ordered revised minutes and future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the May 8, 2023 minutes were insufficient because they did not summarize the complainant's comments, which were read as a roughly 17-minute statement.
allegations.key_passage: By failing to include any summary of the complainant’s statement, the Board created insufficient minutes and violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The May 8, 2023 minutes twice said 'Discussion ensued amongst all present' without summarizing either discussion, which the AG reviewed on its own.
allegations.key_passage: Minutes must include more than a statement that a discussion was held about a specified topic; the minutes must summarize the discussions that were held.

allegations.summary: Complaint sought review of minutes for all 43 water-meter-project meetings since October 2021; the AG declined broad review and limited itself to the May 8 minutes.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review whether all 43 sets of meeting minutes are sufficiently specific as our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

allegations.summary: Complaint raised water meter program issues, including requests for information, an opt-out request, and the Town Clerk's handling of executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review any potential water meter issues, and offer no opinion on whether any actions taken by the Board c ould be a violation of some other law or regulation outside the scope of the Division’s review.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board or Town Clerk failed to timely respond to records requests, including for executive session minutes; the AG said records responses fall under the Public Records Law.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, even if taken as true, these allegations would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Revise and approve the minutes of the May 8, 2023, meeting within thirty (30) days of the letter, in accordance with the guidance provided.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law; similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to revise and approve the minutes of the May 8, 2023, meeting within thirty (30) days of this letter in accordance with the guidance provided above. In addition, we order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
